title: Pairing from repulsive interactions in twisted WSe2 from functional renormalization
authors: Hannes Braun, Dumitru Călugăru, Pietro M. Bonetti, Haoyu Hu, Yan Zhang, Yi Jiang, Quansheng Wu, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan, B. Andrei Bernevig, Michael M. Scherer, Laura Classen
abstract: Motivated by the observation of superconductivity in twisted bilayer WSe$_2$ over an extended range of displacement fields, reaching from the correlated insulator down to zero field, we analyze the correlated electron phases of this system at hole filling $ν= -1$ and twist angle $3.65^\circ$ using Hartree--Fock, random phase approximation, and functional renormalization group calculations. We derive a continuum model with gate-screened Coulomb interaction from first principles and compare its instabilities to those of a realistic three-orbital Wannier model with a Hubbard interaction and an artificial single-orbital Hubbard model. In both cases, we find a superconducting instability of mixed $d$-wave singlet and $p$-wave triplet character, arising adjacent to inter-valley-coherent spin-density-wave order in the phase diagram spanned by displacement field and interaction strength. Our additional analysis of the pairing mechanism points to inter-valley coherent spin fluctuations as the pairing glue. The extent of the pairing regime and the associated critical temperatures depend on the model input, and we trace differences to the interaction range entering the projected interaction. Within the continuum model, the gate-screened Coulomb interaction yields pairing down to zero displacement field, bringing theory into agreement with experiment.
summary: This work analyzes superconductivity in twisted WSe2, showing that pairing arises from inter-valley coherent spin fluctuations acting as the pairing glue. Using FRG and RPA, the authors demonstrate that the superconducting state is a mixed d-wave/p-wave pairing, and their continuum model successfully predicts this superconductivity persists even at zero displacement field, aligning with experimental findings.
main_problem: The study investigates the superconducting instability and pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer WSe2, particularly how superconductivity emerges from repulsive interactions.
main_result: The pairing instability is driven by inter-valley coherent spin fluctuations, leading to a mixed d-wave singlet and p-wave triplet superconducting state. The continuum model successfully predicts superconductivity down to zero displacement field, matching experiments.
method: The authors employ advanced many-body techniques, including Functional Renormalization Group (FRG), Random Phase Approximation (RPA), and Hartree-Fock calculations, comparing results across different theoretical models.
model_or_system: The system is twisted bilayer WSe2 (tWSe2) at hole filling $\nu = -1$. Calculations utilize continuum models derived from first principles, comparing them to realistic three-orbital Wannier models with Hubbard and Coulomb interactions.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), pairing symmetry (mixed d-wave/p-wave), and the presence/strength of inter-valley-coherent spin-density-wave (IVC-SDW) order.
important_parameters: Hole filling $\nu = -1$, twist angle $\theta = 3.65^\circ$, displacement field ($D$), and interaction strength ($10/\epsilon$ or $\alpha$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include the Hubbard approximation (neglecting momentum/orbital dependence) and the assumption that RPA fluctuations capture the main pairing glue contribution.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate FRG phase diagrams showing the competition between IVC-SDW and superconducting regimes, and display the structure of the leading pairing eigenfunction, confirming its d-wave/p-wave mixed character.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares results from multiple theoretical frameworks (HF, RPA, FRG) applied to the tWSe2 system. It first establishes the existence of competing ordered states (SDW) and then pinpoints the pairing glue by comparing FRG results with RPA projections, culminating in the continuum model's agreement with experimental observations.
why_interesting: The detailed theoretical mapping of pairing mechanisms in 2D van der Waals heterostructures using FRG is highly relevant for understanding emergent superconductivity in correlated quantum materials, bridging theory to experimental measurements.
